Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not perform the task.", "input": "we need a handoff prompt for a draft about the luggage desk on the saturday evening at north quay, for the crew taking over after the 13:00 to 21:00 shift on june 14. this is the ferry terminal, not the coach terminal. please make it useful to a desk lead who is coming on after lila chen, with omar ruiz and jo bell helping her today. the purser is nia okafor. i want a practical handoff, not a story about what happened and not a claim that anything is fixed. keep the details below in it, even where we don't know the answer yet.

The main open case is for mara venn. her claim stub is QN418-77. the item is a blue hard-shell suitcase with a brass luggage strap and a green tag marked QN-418. the desk log says its last recorded cart was C-3, but nobody has confirmed that the case is on that cart or that it is still there. There's a route sheet in the desk folder, and its actual note reads “the route sheet shows C-3, not C-8”. don't turn that into a verified location, because it is only what the sheet says. we have arrivals to consider: Tideglass from Aster Point is due at 16:40, then Kestrel from Dunlin is due at 18:05. the time of arrival is relevant because the crew can't check C-3 until after the later unload is cleared.

Mara has been waiting near the blue bench. preserve what she said exactly as “I'm still waiting by the blue bench, and I have the claim stub.” She also said “Please don't send the case to the coach bay; it has a glass jar inside.” keep her warning as a quote, and don't make the glass jar a confirmed piece of desk inventory or change the instruction into permission to move the suitcase. In an earlier conversation with the crew, someone said “We can check C-3 after the 18:05 unload, but not before the crew clears it.” This timing is a real condition for the next step, not just background. don't say that they already checked, or that the crew has cleared it.

There are two other desk notes in the folder that need to be kept word for word as notes, including their lower case wording: “hold the unclaimed cases on rack 2 until the purser signs the count” and “one torn tag was found beside the west counter; owner not identified”. The rack note applies to unclaimed cases in general; it doesn't say Mara's suitcase is unclaimed or on rack 2. The torn-tag note is separate and nobody has matched it to the green tag. Keep those limits clear. The sign-off on the count has not been reported, and we don't have an identified owner for the torn tag.

There is also an arrival-counter detail that may matter for the handoff: the luggage desk has one working handheld scanner, and it was checked out to Omar at 15:10. there isn't a return time in the log. don't state that it is still with him as a fact, and don't invent a second scanner. the desk has a paper claim ledger as well as the electronic entry. the electronic entry for QN418-77 has a blank location field. The paper ledger has the cart C-3 entry, but it doesn't show who entered it. The 15:30 count recorded 12 unclaimed cases on rack 2; it doesn't establish the current count. please keep times and records attached to the right thing and don't merge the different records into one confirmed update.

for the output, ask for a clear, usable shift handoff draft with a short opening identifying the date, place, shift and people involved. then show the known details, the open questions and what the incoming desk lead needs to follow up. distinguish recorded information from things still uncertain, and don't create answers, a successful search, approval, or a final disposition. Keep Mara's request about the coach bay and the condition about waiting until after the 18:05 unload visible. It's fine to phrase the directions cleanly, but don't soften a quote or replace it with a summary. Don't add a policy we haven't given or assume what happens to the case if it isn't found.

include a numbered section for the follow-up sequence. have it say to wait until the 18:05 unload is cleared before checking C-3, and to contact Nia Okafor if the red-tag claim is still not located by 18:20; if it has been located by then, that contact condition doesn't apply. The case in this note has a green tag, not a red tag, so do not quietly treat the 18:20 condition as an instruction about Mara's blue suitcase. Keep the conditional follow-up as written and don't make the two cases the same one. We haven't been told whether any red-tag claim exists or is located. The ending should still have useful handoff content, such as what facts remain unconfirmed for the next lead to check, rather than ending with a made-up resolution. make that last paragraph substantive and part of the handoff, not a separate invented recommendation. organize all of this so the next person can act on the supplied information without confusing a note, a quote, a condition, or an unknown with a confirmed result.", "output": "Create a practical shift handoff draft for the luggage desk at North Quay ferry terminal for Saturday, June 14, covering the 13:00–21:00 shift. The handoff is for the desk lead taking over from Lila Chen. Omar Ruiz and Jo Bell are helping on the shift, and the purser is Nia Okafor. This is the ferry terminal, not the coach terminal. Do not present the handoff as a story, or claim that any issue has been fixed. Retain what is known and make clear what remains unconfirmed.

### Main open case: Mara Venn

Mara Venn’s claim stub is QN418-77. The item is a blue hard-shell suitcase with a brass luggage strap and a green tag marked QN-418. The desk log records C-3 as the last recorded cart, but nobody has confirmed that the suitcase is on C-3 or is still there. The route sheet in the desk folder says “the route sheet shows C-3, not C-8”. Treat that as the sheet’s note, not as a verified location.

Mara has been waiting near the blue bench. Preserve her remarks exactly:

“I'm still waiting by the blue bench, and I have the claim stub.”

“Please don't send the case to the coach bay; it has a glass jar inside.”

Keep her warning as a quote. Do not present the glass jar as confirmed desk inventory or turn her instruction into permission to move the suitcase.

The arrivals relevant to this case are Tideglass from Aster Point, due at 16:40, and Kestrel from Dunlin, due at 18:05. A crew member said, “We can check C-3 after the 18:05 unload, but not before the crew clears it.” Keep this timing as a condition for the next step. Do not state that C-3 has already been checked or that the crew has cleared it.

### Other desk records

Keep these two folder notes word for word, including their lowercase wording:

“hold the unclaimed cases on rack 2 until the purser signs the count”

“one torn tag was found beside the west counter; owner not identified”

The rack note concerns unclaimed cases generally. It does not say that Mara’s suitcase is unclaimed or on rack 2. The torn-tag note is separate; nobody has matched it to the green tag. The count has not been reported as signed, and the torn tag’s owner has not been identified.

The luggage desk has one working handheld scanner. It was checked out to Omar at 15:10, but the log gives no return time. Do not state as fact that it is still with him, and do not invent a second scanner. The desk also has a paper claim ledger and an electronic entry. For QN418-77, the electronic entry’s location field is blank. The paper ledger records cart C-3 but does not show who entered it. The 15:30 count recorded 12 unclaimed cases on rack 2; it does not establish the current count. Keep times and records attached to the correct item, and do not combine separate records into one confirmed update.

### Follow-up sequence

1. Wait until the 18:05 Kestrel unload has been cleared by the crew before checking C-3. Do not report that the check has happened in advance.
2. Contact Nia Okafor if the red-tag claim is still not located by 18:20. If it has been located by then, this contact condition does not apply. It is not known whether a red-tag claim exists or has been located. The case described above has a green tag, not a red tag; do not treat this condition as an instruction about Mara’s blue suitcase.

End with a substantive handoff paragraph identifying the facts that remain unconfirmed for the incoming lead to check. Keep the coach-bay request, the unload-and-clear condition, and the separate red-tag condition visible. Do not invent answers, a successful search, an approval, a final disposition, or a policy about what happens if the case is not found. Preserve the quoted remarks and notes rather than replacing them with summaries. Organize the information so the next desk lead can distinguish records, quotations, conditions, and unknowns from confirmed results."}]
